summary_paragraph: A young woman with a history of tracheobronchomalacia, tracheostomy, and chronic respiratory issues was readmitted after being notified of positive blood cultures from a prior emergency visit. She reported a week of shaking chills, trach site pain, odynophagia, and central chest pain. She was started on IV vancomycin for Staphylococcus lugdunensis bacteremia, confirmed by high-grade positive cultures. Workup included a normal echocardiogram ruling out endocarditis, a CT neck showing stable airway anatomy, and a Doppler ultrasound excluding deep vein thrombosis. A left axillary abscess was aspirated and grew MRSA, but was not the source of bacteremia. She continued home medications for asthma, GERD, depression, and pain, with addition of a lidocaine patch for chest pain. She was discharged on a four-week course of IV vancomycin with vancomycin-heparin port locks, clindamycin cream for hidradenitis suppurativa, and plans for weekly lab monitoring and outpatient follow-up.
